text: That fancy slider on your homepage? Almost nobody clicks it.
Three website myths quietly costing you customers.
Myth one: a rotating slider makes you look premium.
In 2013, a university tracked theirs. About 1% of homepage visitors clicked it.
say: In twenty thirteen, a university tracked theirs. About one percent of homepage visitors clicked it.

text: And almost 9 in 10 of those clicks were on the first slide.
say: And almost nine in ten of those clicks were on the first slide.

text: Fix: one clear headline and one button.
Myth two: a full-screen pop-up the second someone lands gets more sign-ups.
Since 2017, Google has warned that pop-ups covering the page on phones can hurt your rankings.
say: Since twenty seventeen, Google has warned that pop-ups covering the page on phones can hurt your rankings.

text: Fix: a small banner they can ignore.
Myth three: your customers find you on a computer.
Worldwide, most web traffic now comes from phones.
So design for the thumb first, then the desktop.
